planting.note: Set out in spring with the crown planted a couple of inches deep and roots shaded by low companion plants, training onto a trellis, fence, or through a shrub in full sun; this Boskoop Research Station selection is one of the classic golden-flowered tangutica clematis.

directions: Aureolin bears nodding, lantern-shaped golden-yellow flowers with a slight waxy sheen from midsummer into fall, followed by silvery, feathery seed heads that extend the display well past bloom. It is a vigorous, twining vine best grown through a large shrub, over a fence, or up a sturdy trellis in full sun. Prune hard in late winter since it blooms on new growth, and expect self-seeding in favorable conditions, as tangutica types set seed readily. Once well established it tolerates poorer soil and more drought than many large-flowered hybrid clematis.

planting.note: Set out in spring with the crown planted a couple of inches deep and roots shaded by low companion plants, training onto a trellis or fence in full sun; a compact tangutica selection suited to smaller spaces than taller golden clematis.

directions: Radar Love produces abundant nodding, bell-shaped golden-yellow flowers with slightly twisted, pointed tepals across a more compact vine than many tangutica types, making it a good fit for a mailbox post, small obelisk, or container trellis. Decorative silvery seed heads follow the flowers and persist into winter. Grow in full sun on a sturdy support and cut back hard in late winter, since flowering occurs on the current season's growth. It tolerates average garden soil and is more drought-tolerant once established than most large-flowered hybrid clematis.

common_name: Perrin's Pride Clematis (Deep Purple Jackmanii-Group Hybrid)

planting.note: Set out in spring with the crown planted a couple of inches deep and roots shaded by low companion plants, training onto a trellis, obelisk, or fence in full to partial sun; a Jackmanii-group hybrid (Clematis x jackmanii x 'Ville de Lyon').

directions: Perrin's Pride carries large, velvety deep purple flowers four to seven inches across from early to late summer, a hallmark of its Jackmanii-group parentage crossed with the carmine-red 'Ville de Lyon'. The vigorous twining habit makes it well suited to a trellis, arbor, or mixed shrub support in full sun to light shade. As a late large-flowered hybrid it blooms on new growth, so prune back hard in late winter to encourage a full flush of flowers. Keep roots cool and shaded with mulch or low companion plants while the top growth climbs into sun.
